Reasoning:
The subtask requires reorienting the grasped can so that its local -y axis becomes aligned with world +z (upright position), while:
1. Keeping the gripper closed (grasping maintained)
2. Aligning can local -y with world +z (antiparallel to world -z)
3. Keeping the panda_fingertip origin fixed in world frame (no translation)
4. Monitoring gripper effort to confirm grasp

Constraint breakdown:
- freeze_position on panda_fingertip: keep the tool frame origin fixed in world frame during reorientation (constraint 4)
- axis_align: align can_center_frame local -y axis to be codirectional with world +z (i.e., antiparallel to world -z), with tolerance 0.05 rad as specified (constraint 2 & 5)
- close_gripper: maintain gripper closed state throughout (constraint 1)
- manipulator_high_effort condition on close_gripper to represent monitoring finger effort (constraint 6)

Note: The "grasp preservation" (constraint 3) is implicitly enforced by freeze_position on the fingertip combined with close_gripper — if the fingertip doesn't move and the gripper stays closed, the relative pose between can and fingertip is preserved. This cannot be directly encoded as a separate TermAPI term.

The axis_align uses controlled_entity="gripped_object", controlled_target="can_center_frame", reference_basis="world", reference_origin="world", controlled_axis="-y" (can local -y), reference_axis="+z" (world +z), alignment="codirectional", tolerance_rad=0.05.

For freeze_position, controlled_entity="robot_frame", controlled_target="panda_fingertip", tolerance_m=0.005 (small, to keep position fixed).

Logic: all constraints must hold simultaneously, so all use "and".
